text:
matt: Quick sync — GhostSite (customer: Veridian) edge bring-up starts in 30m. Main checklist: seed registry import, BGP peering validation, MTU alignment with customer MPLS, NVidia driver + CUDA validation on A100 nodes, and kubelet node-labeling for gpu-pools. Anyone on call for networking if we hit MTU issues?

lina: I'm around. Can we confirm the customer's firewall will allow our seed S3 pull over the transit proxy? They confirmed outbound 443 but it's intercepted by TLS inspection.

chandra: TL;DR — we have an air-gapped fallback: bring a signed seed bundle on USB via delivery engineer and load into local registry. But first try proxy. If TLS inspection drops SNI, the registry client fails.

matt: Good call. Plan A: try pull through transit proxy. Plan B: offline seed. Plan C: we spin a temporary NAT instance in customer VPC with port 443 egress rule scoped to our registry IP. Need approval from security if we do NAT.

rina-cs: Customer ops (Veridian) just posted that TLS inspection is scheduled to run during their maintenance window ending +1h. They can pause it for 45m if needed.

zach: I can stand by for NAT instance; have a quick terraform module ready: 
```hcl
resource "aws_instance" "egress_nat" {
  ami = "ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0"
  instance_type = "t3.medium"
  tags = { Name = "ghostsite-egress-nat" }
}
```
Will need a customer-provided route to point 0.0.0.0/0 at it.

matt: GPU ops note — node image for this site uses CUDA 12.1 + nvidia-driver 535. Confirmed by chandra last week. After nodejoin run this validation: 
```bash
# gpu smoke test
nvidia-smi || echo "driver missing"
python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'
```
If either fails, don't proceed to quantized model preload.

chandra: Also watch for kubelet MTU mismatch. Customer's VXLAN overlay requires MTU 1450; default node MTU is 1500. If not adjusted we see packet fragmentation and container restarts. Patch nodes with: 
```yaml
# cloud-init snippet
network: |
  ethernets:
    eth0:
      mtu: 1450
```
We should set that in the image or as a daemonset early.

lina: I'll run the BGP checklist pre-flight: verify neighbor IPs, ASNs, MD5 secrets, and route-maps. Quick command to validate established peers: `vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary'` on the edge router.

infra-bot: infra-bot: Kickoff checklist created: https://internal/tasks/TSK-4721. Assigned: matt, lina, zach. Expected duration 1.5h. :rocket:

matt: Cost / capacity note — customer requested 4 A100s reserved. Current provisioning plan maps to 6 gpus across 3 nodes (2 gpus/node) to support headroom. If customer insists on 4, we can downscale to two 2x-A100 nodes but unit cost per-token increases ~12%. Rina, do they have budget flexibility?

rina-cs: Veridian prefers predictable pricing. They'll accept the two-node 4-GPU footprint if we cap burst and enable autoscale off by default. We'll put autoscale policy to manual.

zach: Ops runbook for node labeling and taints (so inference pods land correctly): 
```bash
kubectl label node <name> gpu-type=nvidia-a100
kubectl taint nodes <name> dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
```
Also pre-pull model tarball onto NVMe: `rsync --progress seed:/models/vernacular-v1.tar /var/gpu-models/`

matt: Acceptance tests after bootstrap:
- seed registry import OK (or offline bundle loaded)
- BGP established and routes visible to control-plane
- MTU aligned end-to-end, no fragmentation in 10m pings to 1500B payloads
- nvidia-smi and pytorch smoke pass on all nodes
- kube nodelabels/taints correct
- model prewarm complete and checksums match

chandra: If MTU fails, mitigation = lower overlay MTU or enable jumbo frames on customer infra (unlikely). Our recommended patch is to set host MTU to 1450 and enable iptables MSS clamping in calico: 
```bash
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

lina: I'll be on the console for BGP and routing. matt, I'll ping you 10m before seed pull.

matt: Remote access creds: delivery will use ephemeral acct `veridian-delivery@redwood` SSO. Don't share keys.

rina-cs: I'll confirm customer pause window for TLS inspection. If they pause, we try Plan A. If not, offline seed.

zach: One more: NVMe partitioning — ensure modeldir is mounted with noatime and fadvise defaults. Example fstab: `/dev/nvme1n1p1 /var/gpu-models ext4 defaults,noatime 0 2`

matt: Great. If we hit a blocker we escalate to @eng-oncall. Let's aim for green by EOD. :thumbsup:

chandra: copying checklist to runbook and adding a troubleshooting section for driver/kernel panics.

infra-bot: infra-bot: Checklist step completed: edge-router reachability verified by lina at 1958884410.

matt: thanks team. Starting in 10. I'll post updates here.
